highlights.text: At least she hated me. I’d rather die at the hands of somebody who wanted to kill me, to have it mean something to them.
“Stow that shit.” Crumbs everywhere. “We’ve got problems.” “The same twenty thousand problems we had on our doorstep last night?” Makin asked. “Or new ones?”
Only yesterday every choice came easy. Black or white. Stab Gemt in the neck or don’t. And now? Shades of grey. A man can drown in shades of grey.
“I’ve opened up a lot of men, Gorgoth, and if anything is written there then it’s written red on red and smells bad.”
genealogy can work for me or I can cut down the family tree and make a battering ram. Either way is good.
In other matters too Sir Makin is “almost.” Almost honourable, almost honest. About his friendship, though, there is no almost.
Some pain you can distance yourself from, but a headache sits right where you live.
“Did I fall off my horse?” He must have asked that a thousand times in a row. Crying one moment. Laughing the next. We’re brittle things, us men.
The wind rippled through the long grass. Any place three nations touch will grow well given half a chance. Blood makes for rich soil.
When a game cannot be won, change the game. I read that in the book of Kirk.

Mountains have no memory, no judgments to offer. There’s a purity in the struggle to reach a peak. You leave your world behind and take only what you need. For a creature like me there is nothing closer to redemption.
And if you can surprise your enemy, then surprising yourself is small price to pay.
In the end though, everybody dies, but not everybody lives—the climber, though he may die young, will have lived.

They say that time is a great teacher but unfortunately it kills all its pupils. The mountains are also great teachers, and better still, they let the occasional star pupil live. The mountains teach you to be prepared for change.
I’m not him because we die a little every day and by degrees we’re reborn into different men, older men in the same clothes, with the same scars.
I surprised myself by finding her name. People’s names escape me. Probably because I don’t care about them.
He’s a killer, a hard man, and in bad company he will do bad things, but in half of one hour you will want him to be your friend.

“Old men make old words holy. I say old words are worn out and should be set aside. Take a new bride to bed, not a hag,” I said, thinking of Ekatri. “A fool may scrawl on a slate and if no one has the wit to wipe it clean for a thousand years, the scrawl becomes the wisdom of ages.”
It’s a good enough trick. Say nothing and men feel compelled to fill the silence, even if it’s with things they would rather have kept secret.
I had thought to find a man with fire in him. Ferrakind was more of a fire with a touch of man remaining. He stood in the form of a man but as if fashioned from molten iron

“The Builders tried to break the barriers between thought and matter,” he said. “They made it easier to change the world with a desire. They thinned the walls between life and death, between fire and not-fire, whittled away at the difference between this and that, even here and there.”
“You need to hear such words, Jorg. You need to know that you are loved, not just feared. You need to know it to ease what poisons you.”
“I love you for no good reason, Jorg. I’ve no sons, but if I did I wouldn’t want them to be like you. You’re a vicious bastard at the best of times.”

“These things seem terribly important when you’re young. Matters of the heart and groin. They fill your world at eighteen. But believe me. When you’re the wrong side of forty-five and the past is a bright haze…they’re more important still. Do something. You’re haunted by many ghosts. I know that, though you hide it well.”

There’s something about a fight that makes you forget your troubles. Mainly it’s that all your troubles are suddenly very small in the face of the new problems swinging your way with sharp edges on them.

A small part was that terrible two-edged sword called experience, cutting away at the cruel child I was, carving out whatever man might be yet to come. I promised a better one. Though I have been known to lie.
The thing about the path less travelled is that it is often less travelled for a good reason.
Ghosts can’t hurt men. They can drive them mad. They can torment them to the point at which they take their own lives, but they cannot wound them.
revenge is far less sweet than it promises to be. An empty meal, however long you take over it.
Above those treasures though I left with a message, a mantra if you like. Do not open that box. Open it and my work is undone. Open it and you’re finished. Never open the box.
